cards.title: 0 Hello, kit
cards.text: Three drums make a beat: the kick (a low thump), the snare (a crack) and the hi-hat (a tick). Find them, then play your first beat today.

cards.title: The kit on paper
cards.text: Each row is one drum. Kick at the bottom, snare in the middle, cymbals on top, as on any drum chart. The pads keep the order: kick bottom-left, snare beside it, hat above.

cards.title: The pulse
cards.text: Music has a steady beat you could clap to: the pulse. Count it out loud, 1 2 3 4. Steady matters more than fast.

cards.title: Your result
cards.text: % right: the right pad at the right time. s12: your spread in ms, smaller is steadier. +3ms: a little late on average; minus is early. dyn: how your accents and ghosts sounded.

cards.title: Rests
cards.text: A rest is a beat you count but do not play. Keep counting through it: the next note depends on it.

cards.title: The backbeat
cards.text: The hat keeps time on every beat. Kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4: the backbeat, the heart of almost all pop. Start at L0, no clock, and find the notes.

cards.title: Checkpoints
cards.text: A checkpoint is a short exam of the stage. Pass it and the next stage opens. Can you already play it? Take it now and test out.

cards.title: 1 Eighth notes
cards.text: Two notes per beat: 1 & 2 &. Most rock and pop lives here. By the end: a beat with a kick on any eighth.

cards.title: Eighth notes
cards.text: Split each beat in two: 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &. The & falls exactly halfway. The accent stays on the number.

cards.title: Off-beats
cards.text: The & between beats is the off-beat. Disco and house hats live there: the kick on the beat, the hat answers.

cards.title: Hands
cards.text: R and L name the hand: left pads left hand, right pads right hand. Doubles, RRLL, wake up the weaker hand.

cards.title: Syncopation
cards.text: A note on the & instead of the beat is syncopated: it pushes the groove forward. Count the & out loud.

cards.title: Kick patterns
cards.text: Most rock beats share the hat and the snare and differ in the kick. Learn every kick spot and you can play them all.

cards.title: Open hi-hat
cards.text: An open hat rings longer. On 4& it lifts the bar into the next one.

cards.title: Fills and phrases
cards.text: Music comes in 4-bar phrases. A fill ends one; the crash on the next 1 starts the next. Land the 1.

cards.title: Keep time alone
cards.text: The click drops out. Keep going: the header shows your drift. Bands play without a click.

cards.title: 2 Sixteenths
cards.text: Four notes per beat, and the difference between loud and soft. By the end: a funk groove.

cards.title: Sixteenths
cards.text: Four per beat: 1 e & a. The e and the a sit between the eighths.

cards.title: The four spots
cards.text: Every 16th groove uses four spots. & is halfway, a just before the next beat, e just after the beat: the hardest to feel.

cards.title: 16th figures
cards.text: Three or two sixteenths in a beat: 1-e-&, 1-&-a, 1-e-a. Funk is built from these.

cards.title: Rudiments
cards.text: The drummer's scales: hand patterns behind every fill and groove. Singles, doubles, and the paradiddle, RLRR LRLL.

cards.title: Accents
cards.text: An accent (>) is louder than the notes around it. The skill is coming straight back down. It is judged against your own normal strokes.

cards.title: Ghost notes
cards.text: A ghost note is a very soft stroke, felt more than heard. Funk, hip-hop and house put them between the backbeats so the groove breathes.

cards.title: Your dyn score
cards.text: Notes and time decide whether a take counts. dyn % is how your accents and ghosts sounded: improve it at your own pace. A soft accent is never a wrong note.

cards.title: Between the hats
cards.text: A 16th kick lands where no hat plays. Feel it against the & before it.

cards.title: 3 Ghosts & flams
cards.text: Grooves with real dynamics, a kick line read under steady hands, flams and drags, and 8-bar form.

cards.title: Changing grids
cards.text: Music changes subdivision in the middle of a phrase. The seam between eighths and sixteenths is where time wobbles.

cards.title: Independence
cards.text: The hat and the snare stay, the kick reads something new. Your hands keep time while your eyes read.

cards.title: Linear grooves
cards.text: No two drums ever sound together. The groove becomes a melody passed between your hands.

cards.title: Flams and drags
cards.text: A flam is a soft grace note from the other hand just before the stroke; a drag is two. Written apart here: close them up as you speed up.

cards.title: 8-bar form
cards.text: Two 4-bar phrases: a small fill in bar 4, a bigger one in bar 8. Count the bars.

cards.title: 4 Triplets/swing
cards.text: Three notes per beat, the shuffle, swing and jazz.

cards.title: Triplets
cards.text: Three per beat: 1-trip-let. Round where eighths are square. Hold the beat; only the inside changes.

cards.title: Swing
cards.text: Swing delays every &. 50% is straight, 66% is triplet swing: the swing knob on a drum machine does exactly this.

cards.title: Shuffle
cards.text: Play the first and last of each triplet: 1 _ let. Blues, old rock and half-time grooves live on it.

cards.title: 6/8 and 12/8
cards.text: Count in groups of three: 6/8 is two groups, 12/8 four. 12/8 is a shuffle written exactly.

cards.title: The jazz ride
cards.text: Ride: 1, 2-a, 3, 4-a. The hat foot on 2 and 4. The ride carries the band; the drums answer.

cards.title: Click on 2 and 4
cards.text: Jazz players hear the click as the backbeat. Hear it as 1 and 3 and you have flipped: reset on the count-in.

cards.title: 5 Clave & world
cards.text: One two-bar rhythm organises Latin music. Learn it, then the grooves built on it.

cards.title: Clave
cards.text: A two-bar key: three notes then two (3-2), or the other way round (2-3). Every part fits around it; never play against it.

cards.title: Polyrhythm
cards.text: Two pulses at once: 3 over 2 is three even notes in the time of two. Accent every second triplet and it appears.

cards.title: Latin grooves
cards.text: Dense and two bars long. Start at L0, and keep the clave in your head while you play.

cards.title: Round the kit
cards.text: A rudiment spread over the toms and the snare becomes a fill. Same hands, new sound.

cards.title: 6 Pro
cards.text: Odd bars, shifted beats, feel on purpose, and pro tempos on Strict tight.

cards.title: Odd meters
cards.text: 5/4 and 7/8: count in twos and threes, 1-2 1-2 1-2-3, never up to 7.

cards.title: Groupings
cards.text: Accent every 3rd or 5th sixteenth: the accents slide over the bar line and come home after 3 or 5 bars.

cards.title: Displacement
cards.text: The same beat moved by a sixteenth. You know a beat when you know where every note is, not just its shape.

cards.title: Off-beat click
cards.text: The click only on the &s, or once every two bars. The hardest test of your own time.

cards.title: Feel
cards.text: Behind the beat is relaxed (hip-hop, neo-soul), ahead is urgent (punk). Your mean in ms shows where you sit: now choose it.
